scope: Read-only product recon; artifact write only, explicitly requested by dispatcher
evidenceStage: source-read; no production observation or behavioral execution
authorization: Two explicit owner-approved outcomes; routine extension authorized. No new tool, call, tier, generic thread system, live schedule edit or charter rule proposed.

items.premise: Persisted PersonProfile.working_hours_structured in profile_json is a single workdays[]/hoursStart/hoursEnd/optional timezone window (src/db/people.ts:57). working_hours_auto is separate derived JSON. getEffectiveWorkingHours validates and returns only that uniform window (src/utils/workingHoursDefault.ts:94). Prose working_hours is a note, not scheduling input. Existing update_person_profile schema requires all uniform fields (src/core/assistant.ts:268); write feedback explicitly says different-by-day hours cannot be represented (:99).
items.minimumExtension: Extend the existing structured profile window with day-specific exceptions and retain its existing default window for unspecified days. No new table/tool/service. Use the existing conversational update and authority path, and the existing deterministic availability spine for both slot search and recipient timers. Exact field design belongs to builders. Incremental Tuesday edits must preserve Monday and default. Vague nights do not authorize invented clocks.
consumers: src/utils/attendeeAvailability.ts:273 loads effective hours; :323 currently copies only uniform fields
src/utils/attendeeAvailability.ts:138 complete-slot segments and :165 work intervals currently read uniform clocks
src/utils/responseDeadline.ts:27 uses same intervals for contact timers
src/db/people.ts:2636 owner roster and src/core/assistant.ts:952 memory read share effective renderer
src/memory/capturePass.ts:282 captures prose only; do not silently reinterpret passive notes as scheduling authority

pieces.requirement: Store an explicitly stated Tuesday window while keeping other stated/default days intact.
pieces.whatChanges: src/db/people.ts PersonProfile and src/core/assistant.ts update_person_profile write/echo boundary; reuse existing profile_json, authenticated authority/provenance and update path, plus shared effective-hours reader at src/utils/workingHoursDefault.ts:94. Own the person-data helper extension alongside its consumers; coordinate helper seam with Matchmaker.
pieces.productDecision: Approved: day-specific windows override only their day; unspecified days retain existing default.
pieces.risk: Nested edits can erase siblings or weaken owner/person/auto authority; invalid clocks must never be reported effective.

pieces.requirement: Searches and outreach timing actually honor the stated weekday hours.
pieces.whatChanges: src/utils/attendeeAvailability.ts:138/:165/:323 and scheduling callers carry/use the extended effective window. Reuse dated-zone, fixed working timezone, travel boundary and DST segments, and responseDeadline's shared interval consumption (:27); no independent timer-hours calculator.
pieces.productDecision: Approved day-specific scheduling; preserve existing timezone and travel semantics.
pieces.risk: Partial slot crossing midnight, DST and trip boundaries; descriptions drifting from computed slots; same-day late window must work without broadening unspecified days.

pieces.requirement: Owner can say concrete weekday hours naturally and gets an honest clarification for vague Tuesday nights.
pieces.whatChanges: src/core/assistant.ts:225/:268 tool-description seam and :99 obsolete one-window feedback; reuse current turn's existing tool selection/clarification, no classifier or additional model call. Describe effective state rather than claim note-only writes changed scheduling.
pieces.productDecision: Approved: never invent hours for vague night; exact times settle it.
pieces.risk: Prompt capture proves exposed contract, not model obedience; deterministic invalid-input handling remains upstream.

items.checksRequired: Before/after regression: Mon08-14 Tue10-16 with Wednesday default; incremental Tuesday change retains Monday/default; concrete late Tuesday window; malformed/vague input cannot claim effective clocks; authority rejection; explicit timezone/travel/DST; slot acceptance/rejection and response timer use same window. Preserve existing uniform profile legitimate control. Cross-midnight semantics must be checked against existing interval helper, not invented from 'night'.

items.premise: Each confirmed auto-move creates a durable follow_up/auto_move request (src/skills/calendarHealth/autoMove.ts:200), notifies colleagues (:357), then posts wrench receipt keyed to that request id (:382/:388). Subsequent colleague conversation shadow is keyed to inbound Slack threadTs (src/connectors/slack/postReply.ts:650/:655). shadowNotify's conversation-key cache routes each distinct key to a fresh root (src/utils/shadowNotify.ts:114/:142). Thus move handle and colleague thread are different keys, with no association at these seams. Not already implemented; source proves mechanism, not the screenshot's live occurrence.
items.minimumExtension: Associate related outreach/conversation with its existing durable auto-move handle and anchor its owner-only shadow to the corresponding wrench receipt. Preserve two separate move roots. First related conversation shadow is a reply in its move thread, with later shadows following it. Reuse request/outreach links and existing Connection sends; no generic thread system.

pieces.requirement: The related notification and later colleague reply retain which specific automatic move they belong to.
pieces.whatChanges: Existing request/outreach bridge src/db/jobs.ts:203/:333 and request linkage src/db/requests.ts:157, together with meeting_reschedule context boundary. Reuse getLinkedRequestIdForOutreach src/db/jobs.ts:55 and persisted outreach delivery context; avoid using parent linkage in a way that closes notices when the auto_move resolves.
pieces.productDecision: Approved association per move, never merge two moves or all conversations with one colleague.
pieces.risk: Auto_move is resolved before notices; parent-child cancellation/closure semantics and retry/restart must remain intact. Existing field selection belongs to Registrar.

pieces.requirement: Related shadows use the successful move notice as owner-only thread root.
pieces.whatChanges: src/utils/shadowNotify.ts:56/:114 anchor boundary. Reuse Connection send results, existing owner-DM verification (:170), conversation anchor behavior and history append (:237). Expose only the narrowly needed association/anchor capability to existing producers; no raw Slack SDK or new transport contract needed by premise.
pieces.productDecision: Approved wrench root first, related shadow first follow-up; unrelated shadow behavior unchanged.
pieces.risk: Cache-only anchors lose relation on restart; failed/unconfirmed sends must not produce false roots or duplicate retries; history must let owner ask why/revert without leaking colleague-visible debug content.

pieces.requirement: Each auto-fix notice precedes and owns its related conversation follow-up.
pieces.whatChanges: src/skills/calendarHealth/autoMove.ts:342-388 and src/skills/meetingReschedule.ts:567/:655 supply the existing move identity/anchor to outreach and sequencing boundary. Reuse confirmed calendar readback (:237), closeRequest (:275), M10-masked colleague subject, durable revert outcome, and current notice status values.
pieces.productDecision: Approved separate notices for separate moves; threading change only.
pieces.risk: Current notification loop precedes wrench receipt. Reorder/coordination must retain truthful notified/scheduled/unconfirmed wording and never replay calendar mutation to recover delivery. Corrections from closeMeetingArtifacts must retain relation too.

pieces.requirement: The colleague's related shadow appears in the corresponding auto-fix thread instead of a new top-level conversation.
pieces.whatChanges: src/connectors/slack/postReply.ts:650 and companion media shadow :421 consume proven outreach association when choosing shadow context. Reuse existing combined inbound/outbound shadow, post-gate privacy payload, and native thread delivery. Unrelated colleague turns keep existing conversation keys.
pieces.productDecision: Approved per-move shadow grouping; no change in who gets notified or what reply means.
pieces.risk: Same colleague has two concurrent moves; unrelated or ambiguous replies must not be falsely attached. Image shadows and first reply must choose same anchor.

items.checksRequired: Two moves/two move roots/two related replies yield two threads, not four; verify first-follow-up order, same colleague separate moves, immediate and held notices, correction cascade, unavailable/unconfirmed Connection, restart/retry, shadow disabled, unrelated conversation, owner history and revert identity, privacy in colleague DM/MPIM/channel. No behavior or notification changes beyond grouping. Integrated combined-path Bouncer review after all pieces.
